description: D15 defect 1 — VERIFIED, and it is squattable. `https://koine.dev` is UNREGISTERED: `curl https://koine.dev` fails with 'Could not resolve host' and DNS has no record. That hostname is not decoration — it is the KCB manifest EXTENSION URI (`https://koine.dev/kcb/manifest/0.3`), the stable key by which a conformant consumer identifies the KCB manifest entry inside an A2A AgentCard's `capabilities.extensions[]`. Anyone can register koine.dev today and thereby control the resolution target of koine's identifying URI; there is no recovery once implementations have shipped it. Move the namespace to a **w3id.org permanent identifier** — `https://w3id.org/koine/...` — which is exactly what w3id exists for: a community-run, redirect-only permanent-identifier service whose entries are added by pull request against perma-id/w3id.org, and which never depends on a private domain registration staying renewed. Scope: (1) open the w3id PR (a `koine/` directory with a `.htaccess` redirecting to koine's canonical documentation host) and record the PR reference; (2) change every occurrence of the koine.dev namespace in specs/, decisions/, schemas/, docs/, and ROADMAP.md to the w3id form; (3) specify the TRANSITION — the extension URI is a matching key, so a change is BREAKING for any consumer matching on the old string: state a dual-accept window (consumers MUST accept both, producers MUST emit the w3id form) with an explicit end condition. In-repo occurrences at time of authoring: specs/capability-bus.md (7), decisions/ADR-0007 (2), docs/self-describing-participant.md (1), docs/walkthrough-capability-bus.md (1), schemas/participant-self-description.schema.json (1), schemas/fixtures/participant-self-description.json (1), ROADMAP.md (1). tasks/chief/completed/30-*.json is a HISTORICAL record and MUST NOT be rewritten. Downstream is affected and is NOT this tasklist's work (ADR-0001): a runtime commons pins the same string in at least four places including a byte-for-byte conformance corpus — that migration is the cross-repo tasklist `agora:72-kcb-extension-uri-migration`, which depends on this one. Lifecycle: KCB is candidate (0.3.0); this changes the manifest's identifying URI, so it is a normative change — version bump + dated changelog + the transition clause, Status stays candidate. Agnostic: bind roles, no product names. ROADMAP.md Phase F7 (defect fix — schedule ahead of the rest of the phase).
verify: python3 -c "import json,glob; [json.load(open(f)) for f in glob.glob('schemas/*.json')]; print('schemas ok')"

! grep -rn 'koine[\\]*[.]dev' --exclude-dir=.git specs/ schemas/ docs/ decisions/ ROADMAP.md | grep -vE '^(decisions/ADR-0007-self-describing-participant\.md|specs/capability-bus\.md):' && [ "$(grep -c 'koine[.]dev' specs/capability-bus.md)" = 2 ] && [ "$(grep -c 'koine[.]dev' decisions/ADR-0007-self-describing-participant.md)" = 2 ]

userStories.title: Register the w3id.org/koine namespace and record the reference
userStories.description: Open the pull request that creates the permanent identifier, so the namespace koine is about to standardize on actually resolves and cannot be squatted. w3id.org is redirect-only and community-run: an entry is a directory plus an .htaccess, added by PR against perma-id/w3id.org.
acceptanceCriteria: A pull request against perma-id/w3id.org adds a `koine/` entry whose .htaccess redirects `https://w3id.org/koine/...` to koine's canonical documentation host, with the redirect rules covering at minimum the `kcb/manifest/<version>` path family and a sensible catch-all.

The PR reference (URL or number) and its status are recorded in-repo — in decisions/ADR-0007 or docs/self-describing-participant.md — so a reader can verify the namespace's provenance without asking anyone.

The record states plainly WHY the move happened: koine.dev was verified unregistered on 2026-08-11 (DNS could not resolve), and an unregistered hostname used as an identifying URI is squattable with no recovery path once implementations ship it.
No dependency on any private/instance repo is introduced (CLAUDE.md rule), and the redirect target is a public documentation host.
userStories.notes: w3id PR perma-id/w3id.org#6550 opened 2026-08-13 (OPEN); provenance + rationale recorded in decisions/ADR-0007 amendment log.

userStories.title: Migrate every in-repo occurrence to the w3id form
userStories.description: Replace the koine.dev namespace across the normative and reference surfaces, keeping the version segment convention intact.
acceptanceCriteria: Every occurrence of the koine.dev namespace in specs/, decisions/, schemas/ (including schemas/fixtures/), docs/, and ROADMAP.md is replaced with the `https://w3id.org/koine/...` form, preserving the path and version segment (e.g. `.../kcb/manifest/0.3`); `grep -rn 'koine\.dev'` over those trees returns nothing.
tasks/chief/completed/30-self-describing-participant.json is NOT modified — a completed record is history and describes what was true when it merged.

schemas/participant-self-description.schema.json's description text and schemas/fixtures/participant-self-description.json both carry the new URI, every schema still parses, and the fixture still validates against its schema.
The naming stays agnostic and role-scoped: the URI names koine the specification, not any product or deployment.
userStories.notes: Migrated every live occurrence to https://w3id.org/koine/... (specs, both ADR bodies, docs, schema+fixture, ROADMAP). Two deliberate survivors of the legacy literal, both the record of the retirement itself: ADR-0007's amendment-log Retired row and its 'Why the move happened' paragraph. The schema's `pattern` hid the old host as an escaped regex (koine\\.dev) and was invisible to the tasklist's grep — fixed, fixture re-validated. KCB 0.3.0/0.4.0 changelog entries were NOT rewritten (they record what those versions shipped); ROADMAP's defect lines were reworded rather than substituted. verify[2] narrowed accordingly — see below.

userStories.title: Specify the transition — the extension URI is a matching key
userStories.description: A consumer identifies the KCB manifest by string-matching the extension URI. Changing it is therefore breaking, and the spec must say what a conformant participant does during the window rather than leaving each implementation to guess.
acceptanceCriteria: specs/capability-bus.md §2 states the transition normatively: during the window a consumer MUST accept BOTH the legacy koine.dev URI and the w3id URI as identifying the same KCB manifest extension, and a producer MUST emit the w3id form; the legacy form is deprecated on sight.

The clause names an explicit END CONDITION for the window (a KCB version, or a stated date) rather than leaving it open — the mistake KMI §4.4's edl+json deprecation already made by shipping a transition with no removal date.

capability-bus.md bumps its version with a dated changelog entry describing the namespace move, the reason (unregistered, squattable), and the dual-accept window; Status stays candidate and the existing KCB re-ratification gate is restated, not replaced.

The downstream obligation is named without being performed here: the spec or its changelog notes that implementations pinning the old string must migrate (ADR-0001 — runtime work is downstream), pointing at the cross-repo tasklist agora:72-kcb-extension-uri-migration, including the byte-for-byte conformance corpus that will need regenerating.
userStories.notes: Landed as KCB 0.4.1 §2.3 (new subsection of §2). Dual-accept window: consumer MUST accept both roots as naming the same extension, producer MUST emit w3id, legacy MAY be served as a byte-identical mirror entry (§7.3d), discovery marks it deprecated and ranks it below (§7.3d). END CONDITION is a version, not a date, per §7.3b: legacy root removed at KCB 0.6.0 — 0.6.0 rather than 0.5.0 because 0.5.0 already carries §2.2's removal and stacking two retirements leaves a subscriber that first meets this deprecation no version in which to act. Version bump is a PATCH on purpose: nothing is removed and nothing narrows during the window (read side broadens to two roots), and §7.3c forbids declaring and removing in one publication — same shape as KMI 0.3.1/edl+json; the narrowing is the 0.6.0 minor. That also keeps 0.5.0's already-declared payload (§2.2 removal + the V-1…V-8 fold) untouched. Status stays Candidate on the SAME two gates, restated not replaced. Downstream named, not performed: agora:72-kcb-extension-uri-migration + its byte-for-byte conformance corpus (re-emit and re-hash, not string-substitute), ADR-0001. Mirrors updated: §7.3 mid-window list (two→three surfaces), README/specs/README/ECOSYSTEM tables, CLAUDE.md Current state, ROADMAP re-ratify row + F7 defect row (→ ✅), and both ADR-0007/ADR-0009 spec-effect paragraphs now name 0.4.1 §2.3. verify[2] tightened per US-2's note: sweeps all trees AND asserts exactly 2 legacy occurrences in capability-bus.md (§2.3's Legacy table row + the 0.4.1 changelog entry) and exactly 2 in ADR-0007 (amendment-log Retired row + the 'Why the move happened' paragraph); new verify[4] guards the named end condition.
